 J U D G M E N T

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of .30,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Sri.K.P.Bhavani Shankar,
S/o.Parameshwaran, in road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 11.05.2022 at about 01.00 p.m., the deceased H.P.Bhavani Shankar was going in his Scooter bearing Regn.No.KA-03-HE-8634 along with pillion rider, from Devasandra Junction towards Gowri Apartment on the extreme left side on New BEL Road and when they reached near Tea Shop, Gowri Apartment, Bengaluru, a Car bearing Regn.No.KA-02- MH-8613 driven by its driver, at high speed in a rash and negligent manner,
dashed against the deceased's motor cycle.
Due to said accident, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Thereafter, injured was shifted to M.S.Ramaiah Hospital and then referred to Victoria Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and succumbed to injuries.
The petitioners spent a sum of .2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and working as Supervisor at Lakshmi Gold Palace, Jalahalli Branch, Bengaluru and earning a sum of .40,000/- per month.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners lost bread earning member of the family and put to lot of mental agony.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver.

The respondent No.1 &
2, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
3. In pursuance of notice, both the respondents appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsel and filed separate written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondents have denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondents also denied age, occupation and income of deceased as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondents contended that the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further respondent No.1 is the RC Owner of car and at the time of accident, the car is insured with 2nd respondent.

Further contended that the driver of the car has valid driving license at the time of accident and has validly insured with the 2nd respondent which was valid from 16.09.2021 to 15.09.2022 bearing policy No.R0049531 and deceased himself is responsible for the accident.
The amount claimed by petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.2, in the written statement, admitted the aspect of issue of policy to the car and contended that the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.

Further the car Lakshmi.B vs Sarc Precici Punch on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10194578/
2 was being driven by its driver without possessing valid and effective driving license and FC and does not have valid permit to drive the car as on the date of alleged accident.
Further the injured had also contributed to the cause of alleged accident and was guilty of contributory negligence.
The amount claimed by petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.K.P.Bhavani Shankar succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 11.05.2022 at about 01.00 p.m., on New BEL Road, Near Tea Shop, Gowri Apartment, Bengaluru, when deceased was riding his Scooter bearing Regn.No.KA-02-MH-8613 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

7. In order to substantiate the contention of the petition, the Petitioner No.2/daughter of deceased got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18 and closed evidence of petitioners' side.
On the other hand, the respondent insurance company examined its Deputy Manager as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 & 2 and closed their side evidence.

8. Heard arguments on both sides and perused the materials available on records.
9.

This Tribunal answers the above issues as below:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.1:- It is the case of the petitioners that deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 11.05.2022 at about 01.00 p.m., on New BEL Road, Near Tea Shop, Gowri Apartment, Bengaluru,
when deceased was riding his Scooter bearing Regn.No.KA- 03-HE-8634, due to the rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-02-MH-8613 by its driver.
11.
The Petitioner No.2/daughter of deceased got examined as PW.1.
In the chief-examination, PW.1 deposed that her father was riding the Scooter bearing Regn.No.KA-03-HE-8634 and due to the rash and negligent riding of scooter by its rider, the accident occurred.

In order to prove the accident Lakshmi.B vs Sarc Precici Punch on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10194578/
3 and negligence of the rider of motor cycle, the petitioners produced Ex.P.2 First Information lodged by daughter of deceased by name Kum.Darshini.B with police on 12.05.2022 with respect to the accident occurred on 11.05.2022.
On the basis of first information lodged by rider of motor cycle, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC.
In first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent riding of rider of the motor cycle.
The petitioners furnished the sketch and mahazar which are marked as Ex.P.5 and P.6.
The said documents disclose the aspect of police visiting the spot of accident after registration of FIR.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle.
In the sketch, the offending car is shown to have deviated from its path and collided to the motorcycle driven by the deceased.
The sketch depicts the aspect of deviation in the route by driver of offending car which indicates the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The sketch as well as mahazar discloses negligence on the part of driver of offending car in the cause of accident.

The respondents not placed any satisfactory materials to show that the factual aspects, as described in mahazar and sketch,
differ from actual facts at the place of accident.
Ex . P7 is the notice issued under Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply given to said notice is marked as Ex.P.8.
In Ex.P.7, notice given by I.O, it is mentioned that the offending car has been involved in the accident and negligence on the part of driver of offending car is the cause for the accident.
The respondent No.1 appears to have given reply to the notice which is marked as Ex.P.8.
In the reply to the notice, respondent No.1 does not appear to have denied the aspect of involvement of the car in the accident.
Further, respondent No.1 also does not appear to have denied negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Respondent No.1, being the owner of offending vehicle, could have denied the involvement of car in the accident and negligence of driver of car in the cause of accident.
But, respondent No.1 does not appear to have stated said aspects in the reply given to the notice.

Ex.P.11 is the IMV Report,
wherein the damages caused to both the vehicles are mentioned.

Ex.P3 is the PM report, wherein deceased Sri.Bhavani Shankar.K.P is stated to have died due to respiratory failure as a result of interstitial pneumonitis consequent upon injury to the neck sustained in a road traffic accident.
The I.O., after detailed investigation filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 304(A) of IPC as per Ex.P.4.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending car.
In the final report, there is no mention about negligence on the part of driver of the motorcycle.
The respondents contended that there is contributory negligence on the part of deceased in the cause of accident.
But, no satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to substantiate said contention.
The respondents not placed any satisfactory materials in order to show that the deceased also contributed negligence in the cause of accident.
The documents furnished by petitioners disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of car in the cause of accident.
The respondents not placed any materials in order to rebut or disprove the documents furnished by the petitioners related to the aspect of negligence.
The owner or driver of the car does not appear to have challenged the FIR as well as final report filed by the police against the driver of offending vehicle.
The correctness of investigation does not appear to have been challenged by respondents in any manner.
In the cross examination of PW.1 also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited from the witness.

4 12.
The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioners and to substantiate their contention.
The materials on record do not disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of deceased in the cause of accident.
The contention of respondents related to contributory negligence is not substantiated by sufficient and satisfactory materials.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the documents furnished by the petitioners are to be looked into in order to ascertain the aspect of negligence.
The materials placed before the Tribunal points towards the negligence on the part of driver of offending car in the cause of accident.
So, the oral and documentary evidence placed by the petitioners discloses that the accident was caused due to rash and negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of petitioners coupled with the documents produced before this tribunal, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-02-MH-8613 by its driver and deceased succumbed to injuries.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like age, avocation, income of deceased, conveyance charges, funeral and obsequies, towards of loss of love and affection, etc.

(A) Towards dependency and loss of future earnings:
(i) In the petition the age of the deceased Sri.K.P.Bhavani Shankar is shown as 60 years.
In order to prove age of deceased, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.16 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 18.03.1962.
As per the document furnished by petitioners, the age of the deceased appears to be 60 years at the time of accident.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to dispute or rebut the document furnished by petitioners related to the age of deceased.

In the absence of materials to the contrary,
the document furnished by petitioners is to be considered for ascertaining the age of deceased.
The accident occurred on 11.05.2022.
As per the materials furnished before the Tribunal, the age of deceased was 60 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme court of India in Smt.Sarla Verma case, multiplier applicable in the present case is '09'.
( ii )
The petitioners contended that deceased Sri.K.P.Bhavani Shankar was working as Supervisor at Lakshmi Gold Palace, Jalahalli Branch, Bengaluru and earning a sum of .40,000/- per month.
In order to prove the occupation and income of deceased, the petitioner not produced any documents.
The petitioners not furnished satisfactory materials in order to substantiate their contention related to occupation and income of deceased.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials related to occupation and income of deceased, notional income is to be considered.
By considering the facts and circumstances of case, the notional income of deceased is considered as .15,500/- per month.
In Hem Raj V/s
the Oriental Insurance Company Ltd and others

the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that there cannot be distinction where there is positive evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guess work in the facts and circumstances of a case.
Both the situations stand at the same footing.
In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, the petitioners are entitled for future prospects.

In National Insurance Company Ltd V/s Pranaya Sethi Lakshmi.B vs Sarc Precici Punch on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10194578/
5 and others case the Hon'be Supreme Court held that, in case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 10% of the established income should be warranted where the deceased was aged between 50 to 60 years.

sentences.text: In the case on hand deceased was aged about 60 years.
Hence, in view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioners are entitled for additional 10% to the established income.

The established income of the deceased is .15,500/- and 10% of .15,500/-
is .1,550/-.
So, the total gross income of deceased was .15,500/- + .1,550/- = .17,050/- per month.
As per the materials on record, the deceased Sri.K.P.Bhavani Shankar is married, having wife and daughter.
In order to prove the same, the petitioners have produced notarized copies of Aadhaar cards, ration card and pan cards, which are marked as Ex.P16.
On perusal of the same it reveals that petitioners No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 is the daughter of K P Bhavani Shankar.
The said document discloses the relationship of petitioners with that of the deceased.
The materials on record disclose that petitioners are dependent on the income of deceased.
Hence, petitioner No.1 & 2 are considered as dependents of deceased.

As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Smt.Sarla Verma case where number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/3rd is to be deducted from the gross income of deceased towards his personal expenses and remaining is to be taken as income towards dependency.

Thus, petitioners are entitled to compensation of .12,27,636/-
towards loss of dependency which is calculated as follows:
Calculation Total (In .)
1/3rd of .17,050/- (deduction of .11,367/-
 .5,683/-)
.11,367/- multiply by 12 .1,36,404/-
.1,36,404/- multiply by 09 .12,27,636/-
 Multiplier  (B) Towards Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses; In the case on hand, the date of accident is 11.05.2022.

In view of ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Pranay Sethi case, the petitioners are entitled for additional 10% on conventional heads which is to be enhanced on percentage basis in every three years and the enhancement should be at the rate of 10% in a span of three years.

So, petitioner No.1 & 2, being the wife and daughter of deceased, are entitled for .48,400/- (each) towards loss of Spousal Consortium and Parental Consortium and also entitled for .18,150/- towards loss of estate and .18,150/- towards funeral expenses.
(C) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioners have claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that she took her father for treatment at Hospital.
The petitioners produced 16 medical bills for a sum of .10,979/- marked at Ex.P.12 and 4 medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P.13.
The said documents disclose the aspect of treatment availed by deceased and the expenses incurred in that regard.
The respondent not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the said document.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent and in the cross examination also, nothing to rebut or doubt the medical bills, is elicited.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.
So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,979/- appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of .13,71,715/-.
15.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioners are entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
16. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondent No.1 & 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-02-MH-8613 by its driver.
So, the respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:

7 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of .13,71,715/- (Rupees Thirteen Lakhs Seventy One Thousand Seven Hundred and Fifteen only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Out of the total compensation amount, the petitioner No.1 being the wife of deceased is entitled for 60%, and petitioner No.2 is daughter of deceased is entitled for 40% of the compensation amount.

In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioner No.1 & 2, 60% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1 & 2, and 40% of the amount shall be kept in FD for a period of three years.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioners hereby directed to produce particulars of Bank Account of petitioners,
with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioners, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioners shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioners are entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioners on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to their account after expiry of three years period of deposit, without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Office to draw Award accordingly.
